i0: In sentences about the future, words like ***when, as soon as, before, after, until*** introduce a **time clause**. In the time clause, we use a **present** tense, not *will*: *I'll call you **when** I **get** home.* Not *when I will get home*.
i1: This is the same rule as for *if* in the first conditional. For the difference between *if* and *when*, see [Zero and First Conditional](/blog/grammar/zero-and-first-conditional/#zfc-if-or-when).
ftc-when.t: When, as soon as, before, after + present
ftc-when.s: For the future, use **present simple** after *when, as soon as, before, after, until*: *I'll text you **as soon as** I **arrive**.*
ftc-when.b1: The **main clause** uses a future form (*will, going to*) or an imperative. The **time clause** uses the present: *I'll be ready **when** you **come**.*
ftc-when.b2: Use a comma when the time clause comes first: ***When** I get home, I'll call you.* / *I'll call you **when** I get home.*
ftc-present-perfect.t: When I've finished…: present perfect in time clauses
ftc-present-perfect.s: Use the **present perfect** in a time clause to show that the first action will be **complete** before the second: *I'll call you when I've finished work.*
ftc-present-perfect.b0: *When I **finish** work, I'll call you* and *When I**'ve finished** work, I'll call you* both refer to the future. The present perfect stresses that the first thing will be **completely done** first.
ftc-present-perfect.b1: The present perfect is common with *when, after, as soon as, until, once*: *You can go out **after** you**'ve done** your homework.*
ftc-present-perfect.b2: Don't use the present perfect when the two actions happen at the **same time**: *When I **see** him, I'll tell him.* (not *When I've seen him* if you mean at that moment)
ftc-present-perfect.w0: no will in the time clause
q.ftc-present-perfect-s02: Which sentence stresses that the first action will be complete?
x.ftc-when-b03: Present in the time clause, *will* in the main clause.
q.ftc-present-perfect-b03: Which sentence describes two actions at the same time (not one after the other)?
x.ftc-present-perfect-b08: No *will* in the time clause: *when I've been paid*.
